svg.aria-label: Raft - how ArcadeDB wires it up
svg.text: Raft - how ArcadeDB wires it up
Ports, entry types, the state machine, follower forwarding, snapshots and the tuning knobs

g.text: the state machine IS the database
the state machine IS the database
reads, and where they are served
reads, and where they are served
Clients speak HTTP on 2480. Consensus is a separate Ratis gRPC channel on 2434, peer to peer.
Raft does not replicate pages or a separate store: applying an entry runs the transaction on the local database.
ArcadeStateMachine.applyTransaction decodes the entry and applies it; the snapshot is the set of database files on disk
Data is only one of the eight things that travel the log; users, groups and API tokens travel it too.
SECURITY_USERS_ENTRY / SECURITY_GROUPS_ENTRY / SECURITY_API_TOKENS_ENTRY are node-scoped: no database name, global position only
A write on a follower is not refused outright: it names the leader, and the command is replayed there.
ServerIsNotTheLeaderException.getLeaderAddress() - LeaderCommandForwarder - a null leader address is the retryable case
A peer that cannot be caught up from the retained log is given the whole database instead.
INSTALL_DATABASE_ENTRY; arcadedb.ha.logSegmentSize=64MB bounds what the log retains before a snapshot takes over
A follower read can trail the leader by a round trip, so the tests poll instead of reading once.
leader lease ratio 0.9 for leader reads; followers apply on the next AppendEntries, which is the lag every HA test awaits
Five settings decide how this cluster behaves under stress; the defaults favour resilience over fast failover.
quorum - electionTimeoutMin/Max - logSegmentSize - rpc request timeout 10s - staging timeout 30s
